messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan problem
parts:
J

I closed and reopened R and now it works.

So maybe this needs to be in the instructions.  After installing the package, close R and then reopen it.

Also, print() needs to be fixed:  the headers should be "mean", "se_mean", "sd", …, "n_eff", …
And in the note at the bottom of the print() output, "ESS" should be changed to "n_eff" and "samples" should be changed to "sample".

A

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: log_post
parts:
J

The easiest thing is to simply include log_post as one more variable to save, just throw it on the bottom of the list of variables.  The only issue is that with big models, the log posterior will be a big number in absolute value (e.g., it might be something like -24000) which will make the table look ugly.  Log_post per observation would be fine except that in general we can't really define the number of "observations."  Also it's not really the log posterior, it's really the log joint density, or maybe not even that, given that there are so many different ways to write the model.

But for now let's just go with log_post as an extra row in the table and an extra element in the plot, just the way we did deviance in r2winbugs.  Then later we can think harder about best way of doing this.

A
